A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generalization-measure benchmark, retaining the CIFAR-10/C/P experiments and six measure families despite a changed title and scope. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original hyperparameter-sweep experiments on CIFAR-10/C/P, PACS, and VLCS, plus conditional-dependence analyses and a DistilGPT2/Wikitext-103 experiment in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original CIFAR-10/C/P correlation and sign-error results, together with decision-level selection, sensitivity, cross-shift transfer, and calibration-residualization results.

M1.justification: The CIFAR classifiers and training objectives are retained. V2 introduces source-loss/error-residualized ECE/MCE selector variants in Appendix C.4.2. Appendix A.2 also changes the stated CNN path.norm computation from channel-wise propagation to summed log Frobenius norms; this is a specification revision, without establishing whether earlier implementations were changed.

E1.justification: V2 removes the PACS/VLCS natural-domain experiments and the appendix's DistilGPT2/Wikitext-103 language-modeling experiment. Evaluation is consequently concentrated on CIFAR-10 and its corruption/perturbation targets, substantially reducing domain and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated training-accuracy/loss and clean-validation-accuracy/loss baselines, Random, and Oracle references for decision selection, plus residualized calibration comparators. Its appendix sign-error plots also include full AIC/TIC/WAIC alongside their bias terms, whereas v1's corresponding plots show the bias terms. ATC is discussed but explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds clean-to-shifted degradation targets and decision protocols with fixed selector directions, architecture–sweep–target candidate sets, a source cross-entropy eligibility threshold, normalized regret, and top-k hit rates. Appendix C.3.7 introduces held-out proxy-selection folds. The printed learning-rate grids also change, including NiN's unscaled 3.2 becoming 3.2×10^-2 for SGD; this does not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 expands sign-error analyses to batch-size/dropout axes and clean-to-shifted targets. It adds eligibility-threshold, severity, architecture, and cross-shift transfer checks, plus source-statistics and residualization ablations testing whether calibration contributes beyond source fit. V1's conditional-mutual-information analysis and language-model axis-sensitivity study are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions list CIFAR seeds 0–4, but v2 newly reports bootstrap 95% intervals for granulated scores, selection regret, paired contrasts, and residual associations. It specifies resampling units, including 10,000 bootstrap samples for proxy selection, and qualifies dependence limitations. These additions do not establish increased training repetitions.

E6.justification: V1 has no decision-regret results. Under v2's restricted candidate-pool protocol, Table 1 reports normalized regret of 0.132 for sharpness.magnitude.init, 0.178 for clean validation accuracy, and 0.206 for ECE. V2 adds extensive transfer, residualization, and sensitivity results, changes Figure 1's correlation summaries, and removes the DomainBed, language-model, and conditional-mutual-information results. These are new or revised findings, not demonstrated same-setting training-performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 removes the normalized conditional-mutual-information score K(mu) defined in v1 Appendix C.2 and introduces formal residualization definitions in Equations 57–59. It also corrects the reliability-diagram formula from a sum to a bin average by adding 1/M. Most existing margin, sharpness, and PAC-Bayes mathematics remains unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 makes broad claims about generalization measures across IID/OOD regimes and their usefulness for robustness. V2 restricts its conclusions to controlled CIFAR-10-C/P shifts and the studied CNN architectures, adds decision-level selection as a central contribution, and emphasizes leading individual sharpness/input-gradient signals alongside close, architecture-dependent family results.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's speculative transfer-learning flatness explanation and broad deployment recommendations. It distinguishes association, local reliability, and selection utility; explains why minimizing a generalization gap need not maximize accuracy; and adds substantive limitations concerning eligibility filtering, dependent candidate sets, perturbation sequences, information budgets, and threshold-sensitive calibration findings.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the 80/20 source training/validation split, metric provenance and logging fields, candidate filtering and deduplication, and selector support. Appendix B.1.1 details CIFAR-10-P sequence handling, including 10,000 sequences of 31 frames for the stated Gaussian-noise cell and cell-level aggregation. These disclosures substantially expand reproducibility information without proving that existing splits or loaders changed.

R1.justification: Jiang et al. and Dziugaite et al. remain the principal foundations. V2 adds Garg et al. (2022), explicitly distinguishing ATC's unlabeled-target accuracy estimation from source-only ranking, and adds Hendrycks et al. (2020) and Naganuma et al. (2022). References supporting the removed natural-domain and broader model context are dropped.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, discussion, and limitations are extensively rewritten. The experimental narrative is reorganized into correlation, local reliability, and decision-level evaluation, and the appendices are rebuilt around CIFAR-specific diagnostics. This is a substantial narrative revision beyond terminology and renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, restructures sign-error figures into target-specific architecture panels with additional axes, and adds split correlation views and numerous selection/uncertainty tables. DomainBed and language-model displays disappear, while retained figures receive revised organization and expanded captions.

improvement.justification: V1's model-selection recommendations rely largely on correlations. V2 substantially strengthens their evaluation through direct selection comparisons, source-fit controls, uncertainty reporting, and threshold sensitivity checks, while narrowing conclusions to the evidence. Tables 25 and 49–52 expose why calibration association does not establish stable incremental selection value. Removing natural-domain and language-model experiments reduces breadth, and the new estimates remain exploratory, but the stronger empirical scrutiny and clearer interpretive boundaries resolve an important evidence-to-conclusion gap.
